item.title: Toward Rational Design of Aqueous Battery Membranes Beyond the Selectivity‐Conductivity Trade‐Off
item.description:

Advanced Science | ⭐ Review | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This review uniquely reframes sulfonic-acid membranes as a transferable design platform, extracting general principles beyond redox flow batteries. Its novelty lies in linking structure–transport–manufacturing relationships to overcome the conductivity–selectivity trade-off, while highlighting emerging directions like localized acid placement, biomass-derived membranes, and data-driven design. It offers significant guidance for rational, scalable membrane development across electrochemical energy-storage systems.

Advanced Science | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Roll-to-roll dual-confinement nanocoatings introduce an interface-rectification mechanism combining polymer nanoconfinement with anisotropic carrier relaxation in nanoclay sheets. This scalable coating doubles PEI's discharged energy density at 95% efficiency, raises breakdown strength to 501 MV/m, and extends capacitor lifetime 45-fold at 150°C—enabling high-temperature, high-density polymer capacitive energy storage for wide-bandgap power electronics.

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work introduces a rotation-coupled guest-anion strategy using Mg(OTf)₂ in a PVDF-HFP solid electrolyte, where OTf⁻ acts as a mobile rotator synchronized with Na⁺ hopping. It lowers migration barriers, stabilizes the Na interface, and enables long-cycling solid-state sodium batteries. Screening 20 systems, it identifies anion symmetry and rotational barriers as design criteria.

item.description:

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work uniquely quantifies facet-dependent Zn plating/stripping kinetics using scanning electrochemical cell microscopy, revealing j0(100) > j0(101) > j0(002). It establishes a kinetics–stability trade-off: despite slower charge transfer, the (002) facet yields longest cycling life and best full-cell retention. This links crystallographic control of charge transfer, dissolution topology, and reconstruction to durable Zn anode design.
